ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Robert Peary

code.originalText: Fifteen-week review: neurological recovery, iron, lifelong maintenance and the plan ahead

text.paragraph: Fifteen-week review: neurological recovery, iron and lifelong maintenance. [S]

Admiral Peary returns fifteen weeks after starting treatment. He walks two miles a day with his stick, mostly for safety on rough ground, and has had no falls. The numbness at the ends of his feet is less but has changed little over the past month. He has taken the iron every other day without stomach upset and has given himself every weekly injection. His feet have stayed whole, and podiatry has booked his next visit. He is writing again for several hours a day. His HIV, hepatitis C and hepatitis B tests from the preventive visit were negative, and he was told by phone. He asked whether he could take tablets instead of injections. [S]

list.item:
Pernicious anemia (D51.0). Hemoglobin and MCV normal. Because the cause is autoimmune gastritis, replacement is lifelong. High-dose oral cyanocobalamin, at least 1 mg a day, works for many people, because about 1 percent of a large dose is absorbed without intrinsic factor; with past nerve damage, intramuscular maintenance is the more certain choice, and he chose to stay on injections. [S]
Cyanocobalamin 1,000 micrograms into the muscle every four weeks for life, self-injected.
Blood count in three months, then every year; vitamin B12 levels not rechecked routinely.

Subacute combined degeneration (G32.0). Balance has recovered and vibration is returning; the numbness at the ends of the feet has changed little over the past month and may be partly permanent. [S]
Finish physical therapy with a home program.
Neurological examination at each review.

Iron deficiency (E61.1). Ferritin 64 ng/mL and saturation 27% after seven weeks of oral iron. [S]
Continue ferrous sulfate every other day for three more months, then ferritin and blood count.

Falls (Z91.81). No falls since intake; Timed Up and Go 10 seconds, from 14. [S]
Night lights, the stick on rough ground, and care on ice.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of cobalamin and folate disorders (2014); Vitamin B12 deficiency in over 16s: diagnosis and management (NG239) (2024); AGA Clinical Practice Update on the Diagnosis and Management of Atrophic Gastritis: Expert Review (2021); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, anemia and depression, bipolar, and mood disorders monographs (2026); Guidelines on the prevention of foot ulcers in persons with diabetes (IWGDF 2023 update) (2023); Falls Prevention in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: Interventions (2024); Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023)

Follow-up: Monthly self-injection. Blood count, ferritin and saturation in three months. TSH and blood count yearly. Endoscopy in three years. Podiatry every three months. Second zoster dose by the autumn. [S]
